jobs.title: Director, Planning & Service Management, Strategic Operations & Medical Affairs
jobs.description:
Job Summary

In accordance with the Mission, Vision, Values and strategic direction of PHSA safety, including both patient and employee safety, is a priority and a responsibility shared by everyone at PHSA’s Agencies/ Divisions/ Services, and as such, the requirement to continuously improve quality and safety is inherent in all aspects of this position.

The Director, Strategic Planning & Service Management reports to the Senior Director, Medical Affairs and Operations, C&W and works closely with senior leaders across C&W to develop service and program plans, identify and monitor performance indicators, develop policies and procedures and manage external contracts. Through strategic projects and activities, this role has significant influence on policy and process development related to medical program planning and utilization across C&W.

Duties/Accountabilities

Provides leadership in the development and monitoring of the agency’s service plan with the Ministry of Health, ensuring alignment with the Ministry’s strategic priorities.
In collaboration with the Senior Director, Medical Affairs and Operations and C&W executive leaders, will engage with medical programs to develop operational and strategic plans, annual goals, and objectives, which support the agency’s mandate and are aligned with PHSA and government priorities.
Provides leadership in the integration of administrative, clinical, and human resources information across C&W programs and fosters the creation and use of high quality, meaningful information for planning, service management, quality improvement and decision-making purposes.
Provides leadership for the identification and development of various metrics and key performance indicators for meeting both agency reporting needs and the performance reporting requirements of the PHSA and the PHSA Board, and external parties including the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Mental Health & Addiction, BC Patient Safety & Quality Council and Accreditation Canada. Oversees the routine production of these reports.
Works to build capacity into the information processes and systems for the agency. Oversees the creation of value added information from existing data and provides leadership in the identification of gaps in strategic information by developing business cases and participating in project teams created to address those gaps.
Oversees the delivery of performance improvement consulting and business support services to medical program leaders across C&W. The services delivered include organizing, synthesizing, and analyzing data on patient services, interpreting information, and participating in the development of recommendations for improvements.
Liaises with a range of stakeholders to support the development and implementation of C&W

policies and management of the C&W integrated service planning and evaluation policy framework. Leverages change management skills to enable best practices, policy improvement and systems integration. Key partnerships are with senior leaders throughout the agency, as well as policy leads across the PHSA.

Ensures negotiated financial and service arrangements are in line with organizational standards, practices, guidelines, and budgetary constraints. Maintains key partnerships with executive and senior leaders throughout the agency including PHSA Medical Affairs, Risk Management and PHSA Legal Counsel.
Develops and maintains systems to implement, monitor, and report on deliverables identified in contracts, and to ensure ongoing vendor compliance with terms and conditions.
Represents the agency at PHSA, regional, provincial, and national committees and working groups as appropriate.
Provides professional expertise, advice, and information to others throughout C&W through attendance at meetings and preparation of reports.

Qualifications

A level of education, training and experience equivalent to a Master’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Leadership, or other relevant field plus seven (7) to ten (10) years relevant senior leadership experience in healthcare, quality improvement and/or organizational change.

Knowledge and expertise in quality management and performance improvement. Strong strategic thinking, systems approach, analytical, communication and interpersonal skills required. Superior analytical skills including the ability to comprehend, analyze, and resolve complex issues and present information in concise meaningful ways. Highly developed business writing and verbal communication skills. Ability to facilitate and encourage cooperation between diverse operational groups and skill sets, to work collaboratively to problem-solve and design and implement solutions, and strong negotiation skills to influence others, both internal and external to the organization at various levels. Ability to provide strategic direction and to analyze/resolve problems from a global perspective. Proven ability to effectively manage fiscal resources. Demonstrated ability to use database, spreadsheet and word processing software at an advanced level. Demonstrated ability to exercise tact, good judgment and initiative. Demonstrated ability to manage, mentor and engage staff.

jobs.title: Director, GTM Planning & Compensation
jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Territory Design & Maintenance

Leading territory design and account segmentation, aligning selling resources with company strategy.
Translating revenue targets into coverage models and account assignments, and identifying where the organization is over- or under-covered and what needs to change.
Owning ongoing territory maintenance, including account assignments and in-year territory changes.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.
Fluency in Salesforce data and at least one planning or ICM platform.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The on-target earnings (OTE) salary range for this role is $207,400 to $311,000 reflecting base salary plus variable compensation at 100% attainment. Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

We're a Human and High Performing AI company, meaning we use artificial intelligence to improve all of our operations. In recruitment, AI helps us streamline the process for greater efficiency. However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

We only communicate with candidates through official @clio.com email addresses.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Operations
jobs.description:
About Us

At Seequent, we help organisations to understand the underground, giving the confidence to make better decisions faster.
We build world-leading technology that is at the forefront of Earth sciences, transforming the way our customers work. Every day we help them develop critical mineral resources more sustainably, design and build better infrastructure, source renewable energy, and reduce their impact on the environment.
We operate in 145+ countries while proudly maintaining headquarters in New Zealand.

The Role

Reporting to the Technology Leadership team, this role is responsible for leading Seequent’s Technology Operations function and enabling product engineering teams through secure, scalable, and resilient infrastructure, platforms, and software delivery services. You will drive operational excellence across cloud platforms, developer tooling, application security, and technology operations while partnering closely with Engineering, Product, and Security leaders.

In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To

Define and execute the Technology Operations strategy, aligning reliability, security, resilience, and cost objectives with business and engineering priorities.
Lead the development and operation of shared cloud platforms, CI/CD pipelines, developer tooling, observability capabilities, HPC infrastructure, and AI/ML development environments.
Establish and oversee Seequent’s application security program, embedding secure development practices and vulnerability management across the software delivery lifecycle.
Drive secure, reliable, and scalable build and deployment systems that enable fast and efficient software delivery.
Define and monitor operational performance through service reliability targets, incident management, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Own the operational readiness and security of production and build infrastructure, including monitoring, logging, access controls, and resilience planning.
Partner with Information Security, Legal, and customer-facing teams to support security, privacy, compliance, audits, and customer due diligence requirements.
Lead FinOps and cost optimization initiatives while managing cloud services, SaaS platforms, and engineering productivity tooling.
Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing global Technology Operations organization focused on collaboration, innovation, and operational excellence.

To Be Successful In This Role, You Should Have

A tertiary qualification in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
10+ years of technology leadership experience, ideally leading platform engineering, infrastructure, SRE, operations, or application security teams in a global product organization.
Proven experience building and operating shared technology platforms, including cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, and engineering tooling.
Deep expertise in DevSecOps, secure platform engineering, infrastructure-as-code, application security testing, and modern vulnerability management practices.
Strong knowledge of reliability engineering, incident management, and the use of operational metrics to improve performance and resilience.
Experience supporting security, privacy, compliance, and assurance programs in regulated or audit-driven environments.
Executive-level stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and align leaders across Engineering, Product, and Security.
Exceptional communication and organizational leadership capabilities, with experience building and developing high-performing global teams.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing cloud spend, technology investments, forecasting, and cost optimization programs.

Additional Information

Office-based role requiring attendance in a Seequent office 3 or more days per week.
Tier 3 after-hours support may be required occasionally.
Flexibility in working hours may be required to support collaboration across global time zones.
Responsible for leading a team of managers, senior managers, directors, principals, and technical leaders.
Works closely with cross-functional teams to influence technology strategy and delivery outcomes.

Work Mode:
Office-based

Our Commitment to Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion

At Seequent, we champion the uniqueness of each individual. Our commitment to inclusiveness, equity, and accessibility is fundamental to who we are. If you require accommodation during our recruitment process, please let our Talent Acquisition team know. We are here to ensure a fair opportunity for all.
Research underscores that some individuals, especially women and underrepresented groups, may hesitate to apply for roles if they don't meet every requirement. Please don't count yourself out if you don’t tick every box. We are committed to hiring a diverse team and encourage individuals of all background and abilities to apply. Thank you for considering us as your potential employer; we're excited to see what you can bring to our team!

Benefits of being a Seequenteer and why you’ll love being on our team.

We aspire to be pioneers of positive change in the way organisations work with the underground. We work collaboratively, stay curious, make change happen and have a global impact. We bring our authentic selves to work and are enthusiastic about what we do. Plus, you can expect great benefits; these benefits are unique to each location Seequent resides in. Please ask your Talent Acquisition Specialist.
If this posting gets you excited about joining Seequent please apply now!
For more information about everything Seequent, please visit Seequent.com.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Seequent (Bentley) is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, pregnancy, protected veteran status, religion, national origin, age, genetic information or any other protected characteristic. This commitment extends to all aspects of employment, including, but not limited to, hiring, placement, promotion, compensation, and training. Know Your Rights as an applicant under the law.
Seequent (Bentley) Policy on EEO, Affirmative Action and Pay Transparency Non-Discrimination

Request An Accommodation

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, Seequent is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. We encourage you to request a reasonable accommodation if you are not able to fully use or access our online application system. You can make an accommodation request by sending us an email at disabilityrequest@bentley.com.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Operations
new_jobs.description:
About Us

At Seequent, we help organisations to understand the underground, giving the confidence to make better decisions faster.
We build world-leading technology that is at the forefront of Earth sciences, transforming the way our customers work. Every day we help them develop critical mineral resources more sustainably, design and build better infrastructure, source renewable energy, and reduce their impact on the environment.
We operate in 145+ countries while proudly maintaining headquarters in New Zealand.

The Role

Reporting to the Technology Leadership team, this role is responsible for leading Seequent’s Technology Operations function and enabling product engineering teams through secure, scalable, and resilient infrastructure, platforms, and software delivery services. You will drive operational excellence across cloud platforms, developer tooling, application security, and technology operations while partnering closely with Engineering, Product, and Security leaders.

In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To

Define and execute the Technology Operations strategy, aligning reliability, security, resilience, and cost objectives with business and engineering priorities.
Lead the development and operation of shared cloud platforms, CI/CD pipelines, developer tooling, observability capabilities, HPC infrastructure, and AI/ML development environments.
Establish and oversee Seequent’s application security program, embedding secure development practices and vulnerability management across the software delivery lifecycle.
Drive secure, reliable, and scalable build and deployment systems that enable fast and efficient software delivery.
Define and monitor operational performance through service reliability targets, incident management, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Own the operational readiness and security of production and build infrastructure, including monitoring, logging, access controls, and resilience planning.
Partner with Information Security, Legal, and customer-facing teams to support security, privacy, compliance, audits, and customer due diligence requirements.
Lead FinOps and cost optimization initiatives while managing cloud services, SaaS platforms, and engineering productivity tooling.
Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing global Technology Operations organization focused on collaboration, innovation, and operational excellence.

To Be Successful In This Role, You Should Have

A tertiary qualification in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
10+ years of technology leadership experience, ideally leading platform engineering, infrastructure, SRE, operations, or application security teams in a global product organization.
Proven experience building and operating shared technology platforms, including cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, and engineering tooling.
Deep expertise in DevSecOps, secure platform engineering, infrastructure-as-code, application security testing, and modern vulnerability management practices.
Strong knowledge of reliability engineering, incident management, and the use of operational metrics to improve performance and resilience.
Experience supporting security, privacy, compliance, and assurance programs in regulated or audit-driven environments.
Executive-level stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and align leaders across Engineering, Product, and Security.
Exceptional communication and organizational leadership capabilities, with experience building and developing high-performing global teams.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing cloud spend, technology investments, forecasting, and cost optimization programs.

Additional Information

Office-based role requiring attendance in a Seequent office 3 or more days per week.
Tier 3 after-hours support may be required occasionally.
Flexibility in working hours may be required to support collaboration across global time zones.
Responsible for leading a team of managers, senior managers, directors, principals, and technical leaders.
Works closely with cross-functional teams to influence technology strategy and delivery outcomes.

Work Mode:
Office-based

Our Commitment to Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion

At Seequent, we champion the uniqueness of each individual. Our commitment to inclusiveness, equity, and accessibility is fundamental to who we are. If you require accommodation during our recruitment process, please let our Talent Acquisition team know. We are here to ensure a fair opportunity for all.
Research underscores that some individuals, especially women and underrepresented groups, may hesitate to apply for roles if they don't meet every requirement. Please don't count yourself out if you don’t tick every box. We are committed to hiring a diverse team and encourage individuals of all background and abilities to apply. Thank you for considering us as your potential employer; we're excited to see what you can bring to our team!

Benefits of being a Seequenteer and why you’ll love being on our team.

We aspire to be pioneers of positive change in the way organisations work with the underground. We work collaboratively, stay curious, make change happen and have a global impact. We bring our authentic selves to work and are enthusiastic about what we do. Plus, you can expect great benefits; these benefits are unique to each location Seequent resides in. Please ask your Talent Acquisition Specialist.
If this posting gets you excited about joining Seequent please apply now!
For more information about everything Seequent, please visit Seequent.com.
